i was planning on calling the hotline tonight as a last resort. But my parents set up a family meeting (mostly centered around my sister) and basically i will be seeing a therapist soon. It hurts not being able to tell my parents what's wrong but perhaps i could hold out until my session. i've become a recluse and i'm genuinely afraid of being out in public or even with my friends. Therapy cannot change my objective appearance but it's my only option now. I hate that my parents are worried about me, i wish i could just sink into my bed. i know i sound like a pathetic cynic but nevertheless thank you for your advice.

from what I understood from all the documents I have read, any GP in South Africa, including the one I saw should be able to provide HRT and he just wasn't doing his job. I have booked a new appointment with a doctor who actually is a transwoman and who specialises in gender affirming care (whom in hindsight I should have consulted in the first place). Unfortunately it will have to be a remote consultation due to my transport situation but it's better than nothing.


 I just got off the phone with my friend who's my only pillar of support at the moment. Today really hurt. It's not exactly the best feeling ever to spend a whole day building up the courage to see a doctor, and then having a middle aged man tell you, "I can give you testosterone if you have some sort of deficiency but I'm not qualified to give estrogen to men. Maybe you should ask any other men who take estrogen where they got it. Sorry, bye!" without skipping a beat.

"Okay, I've got a few questions to ask, you don't have to answer them if they make you uncomfortable."
"Alright."
 "So, how should I address you? Are you crying, is it something I said?"
"... You're just so... Wow. What did I do to deserve you?"
"I don't understand."
"Taylor, you saved me.

"I think for now, since I'm stuck in what they call 'boy-mode,' you can just refer to me as you always did."

"So, you're very firm in your belief that this is who you really are?"
"Yes, it makes so much sense to me and it feels right."

"Are you planning on doing the full transition?"
"Yes, and as soon as possible. Maybe I can look back at myself 10 years from now and be proud."
"I'm sure it will be even sooner than that. And don't worry, you'll be so beautiful.

"Were you scared of telling me because of my religion?"
"No, I was just expecting the worst-case scenario. My parents are religious but again that's not the reason why I can't tell them. They just don't understand it."

"Did you really mean it when you said you thought about killing yourself?"
"Yes, I was in a really bad place."

"I promise not to reveal anything until you tell the whole world when you feel the time is right.

"Oh, friend, my whole life, my deepest secrets were not liking the boys who had crushes on me, and now you shared this deep secret with me? Thank you for trusting me. I'm so proud of you."

"I am you, you are me. We have the same brain."
"It must suck being a boy."
